daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Stock Performance Ranking with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using ASX 200 historical stock price data, write a query that calculates for each stock: (1) the cumulative return from the earliest date to most recent date using window functions, (2) rank stocks by return percentile using RANK() and PERCENT_RANK(), (3) identify the date each stock hit its 52-week high using ROW_NUMBER(), and (4) calculate the 30-day moving average of closing price using AVG() with ROWS BETWEEN. Filter for the top 20 performers by return and order by stock symbol. Expected output: stock_symbol, cumulative_return_pct, return_rank, date_52week_high, moving_avg_30day.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning and Feature Engineering
daily_quests.description: Load NSW Road Crash Data from data.nsw.gov.au. Perform the following data cleaning tasks: (1) handle missing values in injury_type and crash_type columns (choose appropriate strategy: drop, forward-fill, or mode-impute based on missingness %), (2) standardise datetime columns to ISO format, (3) remove duplicate records based on crash_id and date combination, (4) create new features: crash_hour (extracted from time), day_of_week, is_weekend flag, and severity_category (bin injury counts into Low/Medium/High), (5) detect and handle outliers in speed_limit and vehicle_count using IQR method. Save cleaned dataset to CSV with data quality report showing row counts before/after and missing % per column.

daily_quests.title: Australian Weather Anomalies Detection Pipeline
daily_quests.description: Build an end-to-end data pipeline: (1) Extract temperature and rainfall data from Bureau of Meteorology / Kaggle weather dataset for 5 major Australian cities over the past 5 years. (2) Use Python/pandas to load, clean, and calculate rolling 30-day average temperatures and cumulative monthly rainfall. Export to a staging table in SQLite. (3) Write SQL queries with CTEs to: identify months where temperature exceeded 2 standard deviations above the 5-year mean (anomalies), rank cities by anomaly frequency, and calculate the YoY (year-over-year) change in average annual rainfall using LAG() window function. (4) Output a final report showing: city, anomaly_month, temp_deviation_stddev, rainfall_yoy_change_pct, and anomaly_rank_by_city. Document your data quality checks.
